Date: 2026-09-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer ask + reseller commission question

Hi Chloe —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Quick follow-up from our procurement team: CloudLane is interested in a private offer on Azure with a two-tier commitment (base + burst). They want the cash price to be competitive vs list, but the reseller wants a 10% pass-through to cover onboarding and co-marketing.

A couple of asks:
- Can Redwood support a bundled list price that yields ~20% take-rate for Microsoft but still allows a 10% reseller pass-through?
- How would overages be handled (monthly true-up vs pre-purchased cushion)? CloudLane prefers a small cushion to avoid billing surprises.

If you can share a sample term sheet or a quick sketch of the pricing waterfall, that would help our legal/procurement.

Best,
Tom
Head of Cloud Partnerships, CloudLane

---

From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer ask + reseller commission question

Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks. Putting a quick sketch below and attaching a one-page term sheet and our usage projection template. High level: we can structure a private offer on Azure with a two-line pricing (Base commitment + burst bucket). To preserve a healthy channel incentive we can:

1) Set list price at the Azure Marketplace SKU level so Azure take-rate remains standard. We apply Redwood-managed discounts off-list in the private offer. This keeps marketplace settlement intact while allowing CloudLane to receive a 10% commission as a reseller credit from Redwood.

2) Overage handling: we recommend a small pre-paid cushion equal to 15% of the base commit that rolls into monthly consumption (first consume cushion, then true-up). That avoids unexpected spikes for CloudLane while keeping accounting simple.

3) Commission flow: Redwood issues a reseller credit against CloudLane invoices monthly; we can also do a one-time onboarding credit to smooth initial months. Credits can be a line-item on settlement reports.

I'll flag Ben and Lauren for the margin math — Ben, can you run a few scenarios (attached usage_projection_q3.xlsx) showing Net Revenue Allocation under three take-rate/discount combinations (conservative / target / aggressive)?

Tom, attaching: 1) 20260916_private_offer_term_sheet.pdf (term sheet draft) 2) usage_projection_q3.xlsx (sample modeling). Also linking a DocuSign preview for the standard commerce addendum.

Next steps: Ben to send the scenarios by EOD tomorrow. If CloudLane buys the cushion model we outlined, we can lock prices for 12 months with quarterly consumption reviews.

—Chloe
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private offer ask + reseller commission question

Chloe / Lauren / Tom —

I ran three scenarios in the attached workbook (conservative / target / aggressive). Summary bullets:
- Conservative: 10% Redwood discount off list, 10% reseller pass-through → Redwood net effective ~0% (breakeven on list take after Azure fees), not sustainable long term.
- Target: 20% Redwood discount off list, 10% reseller pass-through → Redwood net ~7–9% margin after Azure take-rate and channel credits. This is our recommended baseline.
- Aggressive: 30% Redwood discount off list, 10% pass-through → Redwood net margin compresses to low-single digits; acceptable only with heavy volume guarantees or multi-year commit.

On the cushion: a 15% pre-paid cushion covers typical month-to-month variance in CloudLane's usage profile; recommending we bill the cushion as a separate line and allow 6-month drainage before requiring top-up.

Operational notes: to keep settlement clean we should:
- Include per-invoice reseller credits rather than altering marketplace billing flow (easier for audits).
- Provide monthly CSV settlement with line-item mapping to HubSpot deal id (see link).

Tom — if legal needs a redline on the term sheet, send the section numbers you want changed and we can iterate.

—Ben
Director, Marketplaces
